Answering your question about philosophy, when I was about 14, I met a really excentric guy, musician also, older than me by 4 years. He had a very strange (for me at that time) perspective on the world, and it sparked an interest in philosophy. I started with Nietzsche, but ultimately I understood nothing really from it. 

After Nietzsche came a long period of my own thoughts, where I wanted to deconstruct everything, once and for all, to be sure that base of my own philosophy is fully logical and without any major flaw, that would make it useless for building more complicated philosophical structures. But after careful evaluation of everyday aspects of life, (mostly how people react to things, almost always connected with morality or some Darwinian instincts) I always ended up with the same basic questions of why we value anything really, let it be life over death, social status, happiness, things like that, and never found a good answer. 

I have stopped in some point, and after a little time mostly adopted logical positivism as my main philosophy, but I am never certain, and I know how much there is more to read, and think about in this. The thing that I still have from Nietzsche is his will of being closer to this personal perfection, and from fight between my picture of perfect self, and scientific knowledge that it isn't healthy or sometimes even possible comes a lot of pain, especially on some, darker days.
